chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Wasiti, who said:

I wrote to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'A man divorced his wife with the divorce by which she becomes not permissible to him until she marries another husband. So she married a boy who had not yet reached puberty (bed-wet). He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, [she is not permissible] until he reaches adulthood.' So I wrote to him, 'What is the limit of adulthood?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That which obligates the legal penalties (Hudud) upon the believers.'

key_terms.الطَّلَاقَ الَّذِي لَا تَحِلُّ لَهُ: The divorce by which the wife is not permissible to the husband until she marries another
key_terms.لَمْ يَحْتَلِمْ: Had not yet bed-wet (a sign of puberty)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of adulthood (bulugh) for a second husband in the context of Tanzil divorce according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that for the second husband to validly consummate the marriage and permit the first husband, he must reach 'bulugh' defined technically as the age when 'hudud' (legal penalties) become obligatory, rather than relying solely on physical signs like bed-wetting. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on legal maturity (taklif) over mere physical development in determining the validity of the 'Tanzil' condition. The hadith highlights the precision required in applying divorce laws to prevent invalid remarriages.
